Tesla starts Optimus production in Fremont, eyes late-2027 customer deliveries

The Q3 update confirms an early production ramp, while output figures remain undisclosed and hands, durability and AI need further work.

Humanoids Daily ↗22 October 2026English editorial summary
StoryImages 1Videos 1

Manufacturing enters an early ramp

Tesla’s Q3 update says its Fremont Optimus line has started producing robots it calls production-quality. California is classified as an early ramp and Texas as construction. Current weekly output and cumulative production were not disclosed.

A training fleet remains a target

On the October 21 earnings call, Elon Musk described a need for roughly 10,000–20,000 robots to practice and generate experience in Optimus Academy. That is not a completed production total. Training combines human demonstrations with practice on physical robots and in simulation.

Commercial delivery still depends on development

Musk forecasts outside-company deliveries around late 2027, initially for industrial work. Hands, durability and AI behavior need refinement, with AI5 integration targeted around April 2027 if the program stays on schedule. These are forecasts; no household launch date or price was provided.
